guides.title: Coming Back to Prayer After Time Away
guides.summary: Duhaa's signature guide for returning to salah with hope, not guilt.

steps.title: You are not forsaken
steps.body: The fact that you want to come back is a mercy. Begin from hope: Allah did not close the door on you.
steps.transliteration: Ma wadda'aka rabbuka wa ma qala.
steps.translation: Your Lord has not abandoned you, nor has He become hateful.

dalilReferences.note: Surah Ad-Duhaa is Duhaa's hope anchor.
Do not despair of Allah's mercy.

steps.title: Start with today's next prayer
steps.body: Do not wait for a perfect Monday, Ramadan, or a clean emotional state. Check the next prayer time and pray that prayer.

dalilReferences.note: Prayer is tied to appointed times.
When a prayer is missed through sleep or forgetfulness, pray it when remembered.

steps.title: Aim for the five, one prayer at a time
steps.body: The goal is all five daily prayers. The next step is the next salah in front of you. Let one prayer become the bridge to the next.

dalilReferences.note: Allah commands guarding the prayers.
The five daily prayers are among Islam's central obligations.

steps.title: Handle missed prayers carefully
steps.body: For prayers missed through sleep or forgetfulness, pray them when you remember. For a long period away from prayer, scholars discuss details differently; do not freeze. Repent, protect today's prayers, and ask a trusted scholar for a practical qada plan for your case.
steps.madhhabNote: Scholars differ on some details here. Duhaa shows a beginner-safe summary. Follow the position you were taught by a trusted scholar or your madhhab.
steps.scholarNotes: Scholars differ on how long-term missed prayers (qada) should be handled. Pending scholar review.

dalilReferences.note: The explicit text covers sleep and forgetfulness; broader long-term qada details require scholarly review.
Begin with sincere repentance.

steps.title: Make the next prayer easy to reach
steps.body: Put a prayer mat where you see it, keep wudu when you can, set gentle notifications, and choose a simple surah you know. Reduce friction without turning worship into pressure.

dalilReferences.note: The most beloved deeds are those done consistently, even if small.

steps.title: If you miss again, come back again
steps.body: A missed prayer is serious, but it is not an invitation to miss the next one. Make tawbah, pray what needs praying, and return without theatrics.

dalilReferences.note: Do not despair of Allah's mercy.
Allah is pleased with repentance.

steps.title: Ask Allah to help you pray
steps.body: End with asking Allah for help. The prayer life you want is built by Allah's help, then your next honest step.
steps.arabicText: اللَّهُمَّ أَعِنِّي عَلَى ذِكْرِكَ، وَشُكْرِكَ، وَحُسْنِ عِبَادَتِكَ
steps.transliteration: Allahumma a'inni 'ala dhikrika, wa shukrika, wa husni 'ibadatik.
steps.translation: O Allah, help me to remember You, thank You, and worship You well.

dalilReferences.note: The Prophet taught Mu'adh this supplication after prayer.

guides.title: How to Make Wudu
guides.summary: A calm, step-by-step wudu guide from the Qur'an and the Prophet's practice.

steps.title: Begin with intention and Bismillah
steps.body: Make the intention in your heart that this wudu is for purification before prayer. Say Bismillah before you start. The intention is not spoken out loud.
steps.madhhabNote: Scholars differ on some details here. Duhaa shows a beginner-safe summary. Follow the position you were taught by a trusted scholar or your madhhab.
steps.scholarNotes: Madhhabs differ on whether the Bismillah before wudu is obligatory or recommended. Pending scholar review.

dalilReferences.note: Allah commands washing for prayer in this verse.
Used for mentioning Allah's name at the beginning of wudu.

steps.title: Wash both hands
steps.body: Wash both hands up to the wrists, starting with the right. The Sunnah description mentions washing the hands three times before the rest of wudu.

dalilReferences.note: Uthman described the Prophet's wudu, beginning with washing the hands.

steps.title: Rinse the mouth and nose
steps.body: Rinse your mouth, then draw water gently into the nose and blow it out. Do this with care, especially if fasting.

dalilReferences.note: The narration includes rinsing the mouth and nose in the Prophet's wudu.

steps.title: Wash the face
steps.body: Wash the whole face, from the hairline to the chin and from ear to ear. Make sure water reaches the usual face area without harshness.

dalilReferences.note: The verse names washing the face as part of wudu.
The Sunnah description mentions washing the face three times.

steps.title: Wash the arms to the elbows
steps.body: Wash the right arm up to and including the elbow, then the left arm up to and including the elbow.

dalilReferences.note: The verse names washing the hands and arms up to the elbows.
The Sunnah description mentions washing the forearms to the elbows.

steps.title: Wipe the head
steps.body: Wet your hands and wipe over the head. Many scholars include the ears with the head; keep this simple and follow the Sunnah calmly.
steps.madhhabNote: Scholars differ on some details here. Duhaa shows a beginner-safe summary. Follow the position you were taught by a trusted scholar or your madhhab.
steps.scholarNotes: Madhhabs differ on how much of the head must be wiped. Pending scholar review.

dalilReferences.note: The verse names wiping the head.
The Sunnah description includes wiping the head.

steps.title: Wash the feet to the ankles
steps.body: Wash the right foot up to and including the ankle, then the left. Let water reach between the toes and avoid leaving dry spots.

dalilReferences.note: The verse names washing the feet to the ankles.
The Sunnah description mentions washing the feet to the ankles.

steps.title: Finish with the shahadah
steps.body: After completing wudu, say the shahadah. If your wudu was at a bathroom sink, say it after leaving the toilet area when possible.
steps.arabicText: أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ، وَأَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ وَرَسُولُهُ
steps.transliteration: Ashhadu an la ilaha illa Allah, wa anna Muhammadan 'abdullahi wa rasuluh.
steps.translation: I testify that none has the right to be worshipped except Allah, and that Muhammad is the servant of Allah and His Messenger.

dalilReferences.note: The narration mentions this remembrance after wudu.

guides.title: How to Pray — Core Structure
guides.summary: The shared structure of salah, from takbir to taslim.

steps.title: Prepare for salah
steps.body: Make sure the prayer time has entered, you have purification, your body and place are clean, and you face the qibla. Make the intention in your heart.

dalilReferences.note: Prayer is prescribed at appointed times.
Purification is commanded when rising for prayer.
Actions are by intentions.

steps.title: Start with takbir
steps.body: Stand if you are able, raise your hands if following that Sunnah, and say Allahu Akbar to enter the prayer.
steps.madhhabNote: Scholars differ on some details here. Duhaa shows a beginner-safe summary. Follow the position you were taught by a trusted scholar or your madhhab.
steps.scholarNotes: Madhhabs differ on raising the hands and where the hands are placed afterward. Pending scholar review.

dalilReferences.note: The Prophet taught the man to begin prayer with takbir.

steps.title: Recite Quran while standing
steps.body: Recite Surah al-Fatihah in each rak'ah. In the first two rak'ahs, recite another passage after al-Fatihah when appropriate.

dalilReferences.note: No prayer is valid without the Opening of the Book.
Abu Qatadah described reciting al-Fatihah and another surah in the first two rak'ahs.

steps.title: Bow in ruku
steps.body: Say Allahu Akbar and bow until you are settled. Keep your back calm and say the ruku remembrance.
steps.translation: Glory be to my Lord, the Magnificent.

dalilReferences.note: The Prophet taught bowing until calm.
Used for the ruku remembrance.

steps.title: Rise from ruku
steps.body: Rise until standing straight and settled. Say the Sunnah phrases for rising and praising Allah.
steps.arabicText:
سَمِعَ اللَّهُ لِمَنْ حَمِدَهُ
رَبَّنَا وَلَكَ الْحَمْدُ
steps.transliteration: Sami'a Allahu liman hamidah. Rabbana wa laka al-hamd.
steps.translation: Allah hears the one who praises Him. Our Lord, and to You belongs all praise.

dalilReferences.note: The Prophet taught rising until standing straight.
Used for the phrases said when rising from ruku.

steps.title: Prostrate in sujud
steps.body: Say Allahu Akbar and prostrate until you are settled. Prostrate on the known points of prostration and say the sujud remembrance.
steps.translation: Glory be to my Lord, the Most High.

dalilReferences.note: The Prophet taught prostrating until calm.
Used for the sujud remembrance.

steps.title: Sit between the two prostrations
steps.body: Rise from sujud, sit calmly, ask Allah for forgiveness, then make the second sujud.

dalilReferences.note: The Prophet taught sitting between prostrations until calm.
Used for the supplication between the two prostrations.

steps.title: Stand for the next rak'ah
steps.body: After the second sujud, stand for the next rak'ah if more remain. Repeat the same core structure with calmness.

dalilReferences.note: The Prophet said to do this throughout the prayer.
Pray as you have seen the Prophet pray.

steps.title: Sit for tashahhud
steps.body: In the sitting place of the prayer, recite the tashahhud. In the final sitting, send salah on the Prophet ﷺ before ending.
steps.translation: All greetings, prayers, and pure words are for Allah...
steps.madhhabNote: Scholars differ on some details here. Duhaa shows a beginner-safe summary. Follow the position you were taught by a trusted scholar or your madhhab.
steps.scholarNotes: Madhhabs differ on finger movement during tashahhud. Pending scholar review.

dalilReferences.note: Ibn Mas'ud narrated the tashahhud taught by the Prophet.
Used for sending salah on the Prophet ﷺ in the final sitting.

steps.title: End with taslim
steps.body: End the prayer by saying salam to the right and then to the left.
steps.translation: Peace and Allah's mercy be upon you.

dalilReferences.note: Used for the wording and direction of taslim.
The overall prayer is learned from the Prophet's practice.

guides.title: Dhikr After Prayer (Adhkar as-Salah)
guides.summary: A simple post-prayer routine, aligned with the existing Du'as library.

steps.title: Begin with istighfar and peace
steps.body: After salam, say Astaghfirullah three times, then Allahumma Antas-Salam. This is already available in Du'as under After Prayer Adhkar.
steps.arabicText:
أَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ
اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ السَّلَامُ، وَمِنْكَ السَّلَامُ
steps.transliteration: Astaghfirullah. Allahumma anta as-Salam, wa minka as-salam.
steps.translation: I seek Allah's forgiveness. O Allah, You are peace, and from You is peace.

dalilReferences.note: This is the opening remembrance after the obligatory prayer.

steps.title: Say the tawhid remembrance
steps.body: Say the post-prayer tawhid phrases: Allah alone owns dominion and praise; none can withhold what He gives or give what He withholds.
steps.arabicText: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ
steps.transliteration: La ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lah.
steps.translation: None has the right to be worshipped except Allah alone, without partner.

dalilReferences.note: This remembrance appears after the obligatory prayer.
Includes the sincere tawhid wording after prayer.

steps.title: Make tasbih, tahmid, and takbir
steps.body: Use a Sunnah count set from the Du'as library. The common version is Subhanallah 33, Alhamdulillah 33, Allahu Akbar 33, then the closing tawhid phrase once.
steps.arabicText:
سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ
الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ
اللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ
steps.translation: Glory be to Allah. All praise is for Allah. Allah is greater.

dalilReferences.note: The narration gives the post-prayer count and closing phrase.

steps.title: Recite Ayat al-Kursi
steps.body: Recite Ayat al-Kursi once after each obligatory prayer. The full Arabic is available in Du'as > After Prayer Adhkar.

dalilReferences.note: The verse itself is Quranic.
Used by scholars for reciting Ayat al-Kursi after obligatory prayers.

steps.title: Recite the three protective surahs
steps.body: Recite al-Ikhlas, al-Falaq, and an-Nas. The existing Du'as library keeps the full text and the Fajr/Maghrib count note.
steps.arabicText:
قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ
قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ الْفَلَقِ
قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ النَّاسِ
steps.transliteration: Qul huwa Allahu ahad. Qul a'udhu bi-rabbil-falaq. Qul a'udhu bi-rabbin-nas.
steps.translation: Surah al-Ikhlas, Surah al-Falaq, and Surah an-Nas.

dalilReferences.note: Used for reciting the Mu'awwidhat after every prayer.

steps.title: Add the Fajr and Maghrib dhikr
steps.body: After Fajr and Maghrib, add the specific tawhid dhikr ten times. Keep it tied to those two prayers rather than all five.
steps.arabicText: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ
steps.transliteration: La ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lah.
steps.translation: None has the right to be worshipped except Allah alone, without partner.

dalilReferences.note: Used for the Fajr and Maghrib specific ten-count dhikr.

steps.title: Keep it beloved, not burdensome
steps.body: These adhkar are beautiful Sunnah routines after the obligatory prayer. Do what you can consistently, and return gently when you forget.

dalilReferences.note: The most beloved deeds are those done consistently, even if small.

guides.title: Tawbah — Coming Back to Allah
guides.summary: Repentance without despair: stop, return, repair, and keep walking.

steps.title: Start with hope
steps.body: Do not begin tawbah by deciding you are too far gone. Allah calls the servants who exceeded limits not to despair of His mercy.
steps.translation: Do not despair of Allah's mercy.

dalilReferences.note: The verse is the central hope anchor for returning to Allah.

steps.title: Stop the sin
steps.body: When you recognize the sin, leave it. If you fall again later, do not use that fall as proof that tawbah was fake; repent again and keep returning.

dalilReferences.note: Allah commands sincere repentance.

steps.title: Feel regret without self-destruction
steps.body: Regret means your heart is alive. Let it move you back to Allah, not into despair or hiding.

dalilReferences.note: Used for the meaning that regret is repentance.
Regret should not become despair of mercy.

steps.title: Resolve not to return
steps.body: Make a real decision to leave the sin. Remove easy paths back to it where you can, and ask Allah for firmness.

dalilReferences.note: Sincere repentance includes a serious turning back to Allah.

steps.title: Repair people's rights
steps.body: If the sin harmed another person, return rights, seek forgiveness where appropriate, or repair the harm in the safest truthful way.

dalilReferences.note: The hadith urges settling injustices before the Day when wealth will not settle them.

steps.title: Follow with good deeds
steps.body: After tawbah, move. Pray, give, apologize, delete the path back to the sin, call someone good, or do one quiet act Allah loves.

dalilReferences.note: Allah mentions repentance, belief, and righteous deeds.
Allah is pleased with the repentance of His servant.

guides.title: How to Make Ghusl
guides.summary: The full bath for major ritual impurity, taught through the Prophet's Sunnah.

steps.title: Make the intention
steps.body: Intend in your heart to lift major ritual impurity. You do not need to say the intention out loud.

dalilReferences.note: The verse commands full purification when in a state of janabah.
Actions are by intentions.

steps.title: Wash the hands
steps.body: Begin by washing both hands. This keeps the rest of the ghusl clean and follows the prophetic description.

dalilReferences.note: Aishah described the Prophet beginning ghusl by washing his hands.

steps.title: Remove impurity
steps.body: Wash any physical impurity from the private area and anywhere else it reached. Cleanliness comes before the full wash.

dalilReferences.note: Maymunah described the Prophet washing away impurity during ghusl.

steps.title: Make wudu
steps.body: Make wudu as you would for prayer. If you are standing where water gathers, you may delay washing the feet until the end.

dalilReferences.note: The Prophet made wudu as part of ghusl.
Maymunah's report mentions washing the feet after moving from the place of ghusl.

steps.title: Wet the roots of the hair
steps.body: Let water reach the roots of the hair, then pour water over the head. The Sunnah description mentions three handfuls over the head.

dalilReferences.note: The narration mentions moving water through the roots and pouring water over the head three times.

steps.title: Wash the whole body
steps.body: Wash the rest of the body so water reaches all skin. Be attentive to folds, underarms, behind ears, between toes, and anywhere water may miss.

dalilReferences.note: The verse commands full purification from janabah.
The narration ends with pouring water over the whole body.

steps.title: Leave clean and ready
steps.body: If you completed ghusl and did not break wudu during or after it, the ghusl includes purification for prayer. If you did break wudu, make wudu again before praying.

dalilReferences.note: The Prophet's ghusl included wudu within it.

guides.title: How to Make Tayammum
guides.summary: Dry purification when water is unavailable or harmful to use.

steps.title: Use it only when needed
steps.body: Tayammum is for when you cannot find water or cannot safely use it. If water becomes available and you can use it, return to wudu or ghusl.

dalilReferences.note: The verse permits tayammum when water is not found.
The Prophet directed a person in janabah without water to use clean earth.

steps.title: Make the intention
steps.body: Intend purification for prayer in your heart. Tayammum is worship, so begin deliberately and calmly.

dalilReferences.note: Actions are by intentions.

steps.title: Touch clean earth once
steps.body: Place both hands lightly on clean earth, dust, sand, stone, or a clean earthy surface. If there is excess dust, shake or blow it off lightly.
steps.madhhabNote: Scholars differ on some details here. Duhaa shows a beginner-safe summary. Follow the position you were taught by a trusted scholar or your madhhab.
steps.scholarNotes: Madhhabs differ on which surfaces are valid for tayammum. Pending scholar review.

dalilReferences.note: Ammar's narration describes one light strike of the earth.

steps.title: Wipe the face
steps.body: Wipe over the face once with the dusted hands.

dalilReferences.note: The verse names wiping the face for tayammum.
The Prophet said wiping the face and backs of the hands was sufficient.

steps.title: Wipe the hands
steps.body: Wipe the hands once. Keep it simple: face and hands, without turning tayammum into a full wudu.
steps.madhhabNote: Scholars differ on some details here. Duhaa shows a beginner-safe summary. Follow the position you were taught by a trusted scholar or your madhhab.
steps.scholarNotes: Madhhabs differ on how far the arms are wiped in tayammum. Pending scholar review.

dalilReferences.note: The verse names wiping the hands for tayammum.
Ammar's narration describes wiping the hands and face.

guides.title: Mistakes in Prayer & Sujud al-Sahw
guides.summary: Practical decisions for common prayer mistakes without panic.

steps.title: Do not panic
steps.body: A mistake in prayer does not mean you are hopeless or that the whole prayer is automatically lost. Pause, identify what happened, and fix what can be fixed.

dalilReferences.note: The Prophet corrected a shortened prayer and made sujud al-sahw.

steps.title: If you ended early
steps.body: If you gave salam and then realized you missed a rak'ah, stand, complete what was missed, say salam, then make two prostrations of forgetfulness and finish.

dalilReferences.note: In the Dhul-Yadayn incident, the Prophet completed the missing rak'ahs and made sujud al-sahw.

steps.title: If you are unsure of the count
steps.body: If you cannot tell whether you prayed three or four, build on what you are certain of: take the lower number, complete the prayer, then make two prostrations before salam.

dalilReferences.note: The hadith instructs discarding doubt and building on certainty.

steps.title: If one number is more likely
steps.body: If you strongly think one count is correct, act on what seems correct, complete the prayer, say salam, then make two prostrations and say salam again.

dalilReferences.note: The narration teaches seeking what is correct and then prostrating for forgetfulness.

steps.title: If you added something
steps.body: If you accidentally added an extra standing, sitting, ruku, sujud, or rak'ah, return to the prayer order when you notice and make sujud al-sahw.

dalilReferences.note: Sujud al-sahw covers mistakes in the prayer and is tied to completing the prayer correctly.

steps.title: If you forgot the first tashahhud
steps.body: If you stood up after the second rak'ah and forgot the first tashahhud, continue if you are already upright, then make sujud al-sahw before salam.

dalilReferences.note: The Prophet stood after two rak'ahs without sitting, then made two prostrations before salam.

steps.title: How to perform sujud al-sahw
steps.body: Make two prostrations like the normal sujud of prayer, with takbir as you go down and rise. Follow the before-salam or after-salam placement for the mistake type you are applying.
steps.madhhabNote: Scholars differ on some details here. Duhaa shows a beginner-safe summary. Follow the position you were taught by a trusted scholar or your madhhab.
steps.scholarNotes: Madhhabs differ on whether sujud al-sahw is before or after the taslim. Pending scholar review.

dalilReferences.note: The narration describes two prostrations similar to the prayer's prostration.
Mentions two prostrations before salam in the uncertainty case.

guides.title: Differences per Prayer
guides.summary: Rak'ah counts and the main audible/silent differences across the five prayers.

steps.title: Know the rak'ah counts
steps.body: Fajr is 2 rak'ahs. Dhuhr is 4. Asr is 4. Maghrib is 3. Isha is 4. Keep the core structure the same; the count changes.

dalilReferences.note: Aishah narrated that prayers were first prescribed as two rak'ahs, then resident prayers were completed.
Ibn Umar's travel narration mentions Maghrib as three and Isha as two when shortened in travel.

steps.title: Fajr is two audible rak'ahs
steps.body: Fajr has two rak'ahs. The recitation is audible in congregation, and both rak'ahs include al-Fatihah and another recitation.

dalilReferences.note: The Prophet's Friday Fajr recitation shows audible recitation in Fajr.
Abu Qatadah described recitation in Fajr and the first two rak'ahs of other prayers.

steps.title: Dhuhr and Asr are four silent rak'ahs
steps.body: Dhuhr and Asr are four rak'ahs. In the first two, recite al-Fatihah and another passage; in the last two, recite al-Fatihah. Their recitation is silent.

dalilReferences.note: Abu Qatadah described the recitation pattern of Dhuhr and Asr.

steps.title: Maghrib is three rak'ahs
steps.body: Maghrib has three rak'ahs. In congregation, the first two are audible, then the third is silent. Sit for tashahhud after the second and third rak'ah.

dalilReferences.note: The narration mentions Maghrib as three rak'ahs.
Reports of the Prophet's Maghrib recitation show audible recitation in Maghrib.

steps.title: Isha is four rak'ahs
steps.body: Isha has four rak'ahs. In congregation, the first two are audible, then the last two are silent. Sit after the second and final rak'ah.

dalilReferences.note: Aishah's narration anchors resident prayers being completed beyond the original two rak'ahs.
Reports of Isha recitation show audible recitation in Isha.
